result.issueTitle: ORMA Notes — Paws, plants and stormy skies
subjectOptions: Before the next Alpine walk: paws, plants and storms
Two fresh ORMA guides for safer summer walks
Rocky ground, unfamiliar plants, changing skies
result.preheader: Fresh guidance for paws and plants, plus short-lived weather signals across parts of the Alps.
result.introduction: Late-summer walks ask us to notice the small things: the surface under our dogs’ paws, the plants beside the path and the sky overhead. This issue brings together two newly updated ORMA guides and a timely planning note.

sections.heading: Newly updated: Alpine plants and dogs
sections.body: Our Alpine plants guide helps you approach unfamiliar vegetation cautiously, understand which plants need particular care and know what to do if your dog may have eaten one. Plant identification is never certain from appearance alone, so keep unknown plants out of reach and contact a vet when ingestion is suspected.

sections.heading: Protect paws on rocky terrain
sections.body: Sharp limestone and scree can wear pads faster than forest paths. Before and during the walk, check paws regularly, watch for discomfort and match distance to your dog’s conditioning—not just their enthusiasm.

sections.heading: Rain and thunderstorms: check before setting out
sections.body: Current warnings flag rain and thunderstorms in Friuli Venezia Giulia, Trentino-Alto Adige and Veneto, with rain-flood and thunderstorm warnings also affecting Savoie. These are weather signals, not evidence of trail closures. If you’re heading out before they expire, check the latest local forecast and official access information, and be ready to shorten or postpone the walk.

result.closing: Walk gently, keep an eye on your dog, and leave room in the plan to turn back. See you on the trail — ORMA
